# Passive streaming erasure with minimum retained Gaussian memory

Author: `producer-workspace/causal_erasure`, 29 October 2026 Australia/Brisbane.

Status: constructed theorem, independent review pending. This is a finite-bin ideal-receiver result, not a device, noise threshold, numerical bath certificate, or established priority claim.

## Contract and theorem

There are n source qubits with commuting labels z_i=+1 or -1 and accessible bosonic output batches E_1,...,E_T in fixed input order. Batch t has m_t modes and known one-particle features f_{i,t}. After absorbing a common background into the environment state,

    U = G_S sum_z |z><z| tensor W(F_z),
    F_z = direct_sum_t sum_i z_i f_{i,t}.

G_S is a fixed diagonal source unitary to be preserved. Retained mediator displacement must be closed or explicitly accessible to the receiver. A small memory representation or one source observable does not establish closure.

Conventions: Q=a+a†, P=i(a†−a), [Q,P]=2i; Phi(f)=Re(f)^T Q+Im(f)^T P; W(f)=exp(i Phi(f)); omega(f,g)=Im<f,g>. Thus W(f)W(g)=exp(−i omega(f,g))W(f+g).

The receiver uses calibrated passive interferometers, ideal destructive homodyne, retained bosonic modes, and classical records. Its controls depend on known features, not unknown input states. Product local source Z feedback may be accumulated and deferred. There is no added source-to-field coupling. Every quantum ancilla or delay line crossing a cut counts as memory.

The actual record may refine the minimal joint measurement of the n feature quadratures. The comparison preserves the entire refined record of the SAME receiver on the common environment state. It does not claim equality to a smaller-record instrument, return measured modes to their original states, or prepare quadrature eigenstates.

Define Omega_t[i,j]=Im<f_{i,t},f_{j,t}> and K_t=sum_{s<=t}Omega_s. Assume global isotropy K_T=0 exactly.

**Theorem.** An explicit passive receiver and local Z feedback remove W(F_z), preserve G_S, and preserve the complete source/reference/actual-record instrument relative to the common-state receiver for every normal joint input. After batch t, exactly

    r_t=rank(K_t)/2

canonical bosonic modes remain. Peak between-batch memory is max_t r_t <= floor(n/2), with r_0=r_T=0. Incoming modes while being processed are additional; live width at batch t is at most r_{t−1}+m_t.

The count is minimal

**Accept the passive compression lemma, its causal iteration, and the complete refined-record erasure identity at the declared exact model scope.** For fixed finite arrival batches of known controlled-Weyl features with globally vanishing imaginary Gram matrix, the construction retains exactly

\[
r_t=\tfrac12\operatorname{rank}K_t,
\qquad K_t=\sum_{s\le t}\operatorname{Im}(F_s^\dagger F_s)
\]

canonical bosonic modes after cut \(t\). It uses passive mode mixing, destructive homodyne and local diagonal source feedback, without extra source-to-field interaction. Gaussian, vacuum, thermal and factorized input-state assumptions are unnecessary for the exact identity.

**Accept the matching lower bound within the explicitly declared noiseless linear Gaussian reconstruction class.** This is not a minimum over arbitrary non-Gaussian receivers, modular Weyl measurements, arbitrary Hilbert-space encodings, or approximate state-restricted recovery. All quantum ancillas, delay lines and bypasses crossing a cut must count.

Canonical-mode count is not finite Hilbert dimension, energy capacity, lifetime, record precision or total hardware cost. Live width includes incoming modes. Exact feature knowledge and ideal sharp homodyne remain supplied interfaces. The numerical compiler residuals are not physical channel-error certificates.

# Energy-restricted approximate passive compilation

Root corollary, 29 October 2026. This supplies a finite-error interface to the exact receiver theorem; its exact rank minimum is not a physical finite-error lower bound. Review is separate.

Let Y have complex-orthonormal columns representing the receiver's measured mode/quadrature axes, with unused modes discarded. In the W(f)=exp[i Phi(f)] convention define

    ftilde_i=Y Re(Y†f_i), Delta_i=f_i-ftilde_i.

The ftilde_i are isotropic. The same receiver, with local feedback coefficients Re(Y†f_i), exactly erases their controlled family. Y may be a refined causal receiver; its physical chronology still applies.

For each source label z let Ftilde_z=sum z_i ftilde_i, Delta_z=sum z_i Delta_i, phi_z=Im<Ftilde_z,Delta_z>. Suppose the common pre-displacement input, including source/reference correlations, has total field number moment <N><=E. Put

    d=max_z ||Delta_z||,
    b=inf_c max_z |exp[i(phi_z-c)]-1|.

Then the corrected source/reference/ACTUAL-record instrument is within complete half trace distance

    min(1, d(sqrt(E)+sqrt(E+1))+b)                         (1)

of the intended diagonal gate and the same common receiver instrument. A separate source-phase or common-background comparison is additive. This is an energy-constrained supremum, not unrestricted diamond distance.

## Proof

W(Ftilde_z+Delta_z)=exp[i phi_z]W(Ftilde_z)W(Delta_z). For any purification psi=sum_z |z>psi_z,

    sum_z ||a(Delta_z)psi_z||²<=d²E,
    sum_z ||a†(Delta_z)psi_z||²<=d²(E+1).

Integrating the unitary group generated by controlled Phi(Delta_z) bounds its vector difference from identity by d(sqrt(E)+sqrt(E+1)). Removing an arbitrary GLOBAL phase exp(ic) leaves additional error at most b. Pure-state half trace distance is at most vector distance. Purification and contractivity through the common detector/feedback prove (1). No per-branch energy assumption or source-field independence was introduced. The source-dependent Weyl phase was not silently treated as free local feedback.
